compiled_state.description:
## Context

A deterministic two-process harness confirms that `sync.reconverge` inspects tracker recovery markers before acquiring the store write lock. Process A performs the non-fast-forward push recovery merge introduced under `cindery-lithe-acaciarat`. It owns the write lock while Git creates `MERGE_HEAD`. Process B calls `sync.reconverge`, sees that marker at the pre-lock early exit, emits an `fsck-recover` warning, and returns without waiting for the lock.

Process A then completes successfully. Its merge marker and lock clear, and the local and remote tips match. The warning therefore diagnoses an abandoned recovery state when the marker belongs to the process that owns the lock. The skipped reconvergence round also delays freshness. The enrichment drain is not involved.

The harness is `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-debug-harness-20260824/h1_stage3.py`. Its SHA-256 is `e65c356bdc288c8729d5170524b89daca01e667600c2b385e4211c50e6083764`.

`cindery-lithe-acaciarat` correctly moved the push recovery merge under the write lock and added an in-lock recovery check. Its plan review explicitly preserved the existing pre-lock check as an early exit. That check predates the lock-owned push recovery interaction and cannot distinguish a stranded merge from work performed by the lock holder.

## Plan

- Make recovery-state classification in `sync.reconverge` authoritative only after the store write lock is acquired.
- Preserve fetch outside the store write lock.
- Preserve the in-lock `check_no_rebase_in_progress` guard in `_do_reconverge`.
- Add a deterministic concurrency test with state-based barriers. Pause a push recovery merge after `MERGE_HEAD` appears, start a peer reconverge, confirm that it remains pending, then release the merge.
- Preserve refusal and recovery guidance when a merge marker remains after lock acquisition.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A peer reconverge does not return or emit an `fsck-recover` warning solely because a lock-owning push recovery merge has created `MERGE_HEAD`.
- [ ] After the push recovery merge releases the lock, both operations exit successfully, `MERGE_HEAD` is absent, the lock is clear, local and remote tips match, and all seeded events remain reachable.
- [ ] A stranded merge marker found after lock acquisition still blocks reset or merge mutation and directs the operator to `rebar fsck-recover`.
- [ ] Fetch remains outside the store write lock, and existing fetch coordination and best-effort lock timeout behavior remain unchanged.
- [ ] The regression test uses synchronization barriers instead of a wall-clock race.
- [ ] Focused tests, lint, type checking, and the full suite pass.

file_impact.reason: Move authoritative recovery-state classification under the store write lock without moving fetch.
Prove a peer reconverge waits for a lock-owned push recovery merge and preserves events.
Preserve stranded-merge refusal and fetch timeout behavior.

compiled_state.title: sync.reconverge misclassifies a lock-owned push recovery merge as abandoned
